+def test_fused_recurrent_varlen(
+    H: int,

+    dtype: torch.dtype,

+    N, T = len(cu_seqlens) - 1, cu_seqlens[-1]
+    q = torch.randn(1, T, H, K, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=True)
+    k = torch.randn(1, T, H, K, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=True)
+    v = torch.randn(1, T, H, V, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=True)

+    outputs, states = [], []

+            v=v[:, start:end],
+            a=a[:, start:end],

## Summary

Fixes #1393, reported by @RoelsJonas. Packed variable-length IPLR calls requesting a final state now allocate one state per sequence, matching the kernel grid instead of the flattened batch size. Dense calls are unchanged.

Replaces #1396 at @zhiyuan1i's request after the maintainer-side history incident; the original production fix `8b31be78` is retained, with a subsequent test-only follow-up. Previous discussion: https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/pull/1396#issuecomment-6195045461.

## Test plan

Current test-only follow-up follows the review in https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/pull/1419#issuecomment-6232459889: typed `(H, K, V, cu_seqlens, dtype)` cases and descriptive IDs, Python-list boundaries for the per-sequence reference, explicit checks of every supported input gradient, both initial-state modes, and unchanged `0.003` tolerances. The original short and D=100 cases remain; new cases cover one packed sequence, K=32/V=48 with a partial value tile, and an empty middle sequence with an exact initialized-state check. Dense/chunk tests and all production code are unchanged by this follow-up. The full file now defines 24 parameterized cases (10 varlen and 14 existing cases).

Current validation: all applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including pinned Ruff 0.14.10 and autopep8 2.3.2; `git diff --check` and the dependency helper passed. An AST comparison confirms all other tests are unchanged.

**Current-head GPU validation passed on `29f4364a918a0a7dd27635d7b8d806b75204d25d`: 24 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped in 175.61 seconds.** Run on 2026-10-17 using one NVIDIA GB200, driver 580.167.08, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.11.0.post1+cu132.msh (CUDA 13.2), Triton 3.6.0, Transformers 5.4.0, and einops 0.8.2. The source snapshot was verified before execution; `FLA_CI_ENV=0`, the standard NaN-allocation fixture, and all existing numerical tolerances were retained. The 10 packed cases and all 14 existing dense/chunk cases passed. The 14 warnings are PyTorch `torch.jit.script_method` deprecation warnings.

```bash
FLA_CI_ENV=0 python -m pytest tests/ops/test_iplr_delta.py -q
```

The dependency helper also reports `test_gdn2.py` through package imports; it has no IPLR callsite and was not rerun. Other accelerator platforms and compute-sanitizer were not run.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence on 8b31be78 (not validation of the current test follow-up)</summary>

Existing validation of unchanged commit `8b31be78` against base `3995fd79` on RTX 5090, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0, with `FLA_CI_ENV=0`:

```bash
python scripts/find_dependent_tests.py fla/ops/generalized_delta_rule/iplr/fused_recurrent.py
FLA_CI_ENV=0 python -m pytest tests/ops/test_iplr_delta.py -q
```

18 passed, zero failed/skipped. The packed-sequence cases compare outputs, final states and all supported gradients against the existing per-sequence reference, with/without initial states and partial dimensions. Existing tolerances and the NaN allocation fixture remain enabled. One unrelated pytest assertion-rewrite warning for `anyio` was emitted.

A separate prelaunch allocation probe on the real public wrapper records the old two-sequence allocation as `(1, 2, 16, 16)` instead of `(2, 2, 16, 16)`; dense and single-sequence controls match. All three allocations match after the fix. The probe intercepts allocation before launch: the unsafe baseline CUDA write and compute-sanitizer were not run.

The dependency helper also lists `test_gdn2.py` through package imports; that suite was not run, and no IPLR call was found there. Other accelerators and full pre-commit are unrun; lint remains for CI. On resubmission, the dependency helper and `git diff --check` pass, and the restored main comparison contains only the intended two files / one commit. GPU tests were not rerun for this unchanged head.

</details>

## Benchmark / NCU

N/A: this corrects host-side final-state allocation and its shape documentation; the Triton kernels, launch grid and numerical algorithm are unchanged. No speedup claim. The invalid varlen baseline was not benchmarked.

## Breaking changes

None. This restores the documented per-sequence state contract for packed inputs.

- [x] Kernel changes include same-hardware before/after benchmark numbers, dense + varlen where applicable (tick as N/A when no kernel code changed).
- [ ] This PR is minor/cosmetic-only (typo, formatting, style-only tweaks) — tick only if it is, and justify below.
- [ ] I understand this PR exceeds 500 changed lines and have explained its single purpose and why it should stay together below.

sources.author_assertions:
## What Problem This Solves

Dispatching concurrent workspaces to one node repeatedly walks and hashes the same installed worker bundle. The launch-wire scenario dispatches twelve workspaces against a bundle with thousands of files, making redundant integrity scans a significant source of work near its existing timeout.

## User Impact

Concurrent workspace installs share one in-progress integrity scan when the same bundle has already been prewarmed. Later requests still verify the installed files and repair corruption. No timeout, integrity requirement, credential boundary, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node-host installer owns the sharing. It keys by Gateway namespace and the complete existing build identity, keeps scans on its namespace queue, and discards the shared promise on settlement. Retention and possible replacement invalidate sharing before joining that queue. Each caller retains its own cancellation outcome and successful-install bookkeeping; downloads and prewarm keep their existing caller custody.

A permanent hash-only cache would be unsafe because installed directories remain mutable. This deliberately coalesces overlapping checks only; cold installs and bundles not yet prewarmed retain their existing behavior. The existing per-workspace repeated warm scan is replaced by this shared read, without adding a second integrity implementation.

Accepted edge: callers already overlapping one scan share that observation of the installed files; no trust persists after the scan settles. Every existing ownership, manifest, hash, containment, and archive validation remains in place. No security checks were removed.

## Evidence

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full installed-directory scans for twelve overlapping prewarmed installs | 12 | 1 |
| SQLite calls / requests added by this owner | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Gateway main-thread SQLite (T1) in touched owner | 0 | 0 |
| Twelve-workspace dispatch and full launch-wire wall time | Unmeasured on a qualified host | Unmeasured on a qualified host |

The regression fails on the base with twelve scans instead of one. All 35 candidate owner tests pass, including independent caller cancellation, same-length on-disk tampering repair, transfer/resume, rollback, nested dependency tampering, and platform modes. The retention-order regression also passes. The private QA runtime build passes; The [exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39022633884) passes, including the node-worker E2E selection containing launch-wire; the 240-second test timeout is unchanged. No warmed-turn SQL claim: this lane changes filesystem bundle installation only.

Codex autoreview: scoped clean through P2, one round. Focused formatting, basic lint, and diff whitespace checks pass. CI types, type-aware lint, source contracts, architecture/Madge, and database/worker/dialect ratchets pass. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` is green. Knip fails with exactly the same 16 findings on the candidate and current main `47b99c6c2727bc94b2db75bf6c94b047e0052999` (7 production, 8 full-tree, 1 generated declaration); these are inherited, with no findings in the changed owner. No schema, SDK, update/Doctor, plugin loading, or service-lifecycle change; published-driver update cell is not applicable.

The available local host is heavily loaded. An immediate Testbox attempt queued and was cancelled; its lease and campaign slot are released. The requested three alternating timing pairs were not run on this saturated host. No latency improvement is claimed. The duplicate local E2E runner was cancelled while waiting for a proof slot. In the single candidate CI run, launch-wire passed in 69.951 seconds and its twelve-workspace dispatch phase took 3.317 seconds (phase markers 37.850 -> 41.167 seconds). These are candidate-only observations, not a before/after latency claim.

Review follow-up: alternating old/new builds in one namespace can evict the single pending slot and cause extra scans. Build mismatches still validate independently, so this affects only the optimization hit rate. This PR targets the observed same-build dispatch batch; retaining pending scans for multiple concurrent builds is deferred, with no correctness or integrity bypass.

Change size: production +66/-24 lines, tests +102, docs +2. Growth is the bounded in-flight map and invalidation needed to avoid caching mutable files or sharing caller-specific effects.
